name: Reservoir Square
note: 'The first park at the site was opened in 1847 and was called Reservoir Square due to its proximity to the Croton Distributing Reservoir.' (Crystal Palace 1853-58 on the square.)

name: Bryant Park
note: 'The square was renamed in 1884 for abolitionist and journalist William Cullen Bryant.'

name: Washington Parade Ground
note: 'In 1826 ... the city bought the land west of Minetta Creek, the square was laid out and leveled, and it was turned into the Washington Military Parade Ground.' Label shortened; end year = the first park (next row).

name: Washington Square Park
note: 'In 1849 and 1850, the parade ground was reworked into the first park on the site.' The name Washington Square was in use for the place before that; the change of label is dated to the park (estimated).

name: East River Park
note: 'The section of the park lying south of 86th Street (set aside as East River Park in 1876)'; northern section acquired 1891.

name: Carl Schurz Park
note: 'East River Park was renamed Carl Schurz Park in 1911.' (NYC Parks dates the naming by the Board of Aldermen to 1910.)

name: Mount Morris Park
note: 'Created in 1840 ... When the park was opened to the public in 1840' as Mount Morris Park (Mount Morris Square).

name: Marcus Garvey Park
note: 'City Council voted to officially rename the park to Marcus Garvey Memorial Park in 1973, during the same vote in which Welfare Island was renamed Roosevelt Island.'

name: Washington Park
note: 'in 1847 established what was then called Washington Park, Brooklyn's second park, after City Park (today's Commodore Barry Park)'.

name: Fort Greene Park
note: Renamed Fort Greene Park in 1897 (NYC Parks history page, which refuses automated requests: year as given in the project brief, NOT read from the page here).

name: City Park
note: 'The park was acquired in 1836 by the Village of Brooklyn ... When first acquired, it was called City Park.' The oldest park in Brooklyn.

name: Commodore Barry Park
note: 'it was named for Commodore John Barry in 1951 due to its location next to the Brooklyn Navy Yard that Barry helped found'.

name: Flushing Meadow Park
note: 'In 1935, the site, now planned as Flushing Meadow Park, was selected for what would become the 1939 World's Fair.' Label from the fair's opening (parks.csv).

name: Flushing Meadows–Corona Park
note: 'In early 1964, the New York City Council added Corona to the park's name; the park was now named Flushing Meadows-Corona Park, in preparation for that year's World's Fair.'

name: Mulberry Bend Park
note: Chinatown, on the cleared Mulberry Bend of the Five Points: 'formerly known as Mulberry Bend Park, Five Points Park and Paradise Park ... built in 1897'. (Point given: Brooklyn has a Columbus Park too.)

name: Columbus Park
note: 'In 1911 ... a redesign of the park, which was then renamed Columbus Park.'

name: Williamsburg Park
note: 'The park was known as Williamsburg Park from 1903 to 1906' (land acquired 1903; the park opened 1906, so parks.csv starts it then and this label does not show).

name: Greenpoint Park
note: 'Opened in 1906 and originally named Greenpoint Park'.

name: McCarren Park
note: 'renamed McCarren Park in 1909 after State Senator Patrick H. McCarren'.

name: Tompkins Park
note: 'In June 1857, the Common Council of the City of Brooklyn voted to establish Tompkins Park, making it the first park established by the city of Brooklyn.'

name: Herbert Von King Park
note: 'renamed in 1985 in honor of Herbert Von King, a longtime local community organizer'.

name: Colonial Park
note: 'The land for the park was acquired from 1894 to 1899 and the first section opened in 1911 as Colonial Park.' No label before 1911.

name: Jackie Robinson Park
note: 'The park was renamed after baseball player Jackie Robinson in 1978.'

name: Hillside Park
note: 'New York City acquired land to build a park, named Hillside Park, in 1928.'

name: Cunningham Park
note: 'In 1935, the Board of Aldermen voted in favor of renaming Hillside Park in honor of Cunningham.'

name: Bushwick Park
note: 'Previously, this was known as Bushwick Park ... transformed into a showplace park by 1896.' Start = the Parks acquisition year 1890.

name: Maria Hernandez Park
note: ESTIMATED 1989: 'On August 8, 1989, Maria was shot ... the park was renamed in her honor' (the year of the renaming itself is not stated).

name: Hudson Square
note: Vanished park (no outline today): 'in 1803 Trinity began building St. John's Chapel and laid out Hudson Square, creating New York City's first development of townhouses around a private park'; 'bounded by Varick Street, Laight Street, Hudson Street and Beach Street'. Point = centre of that block.

name: St. John's Park
note: 'By 1827, the neighborhood had become known as St. John's Park'; 'In 1866, it was sold to Cornelius Vanderbilt's Hudson River Railway Company' for the freight depot (end 1867 as in parks.csv).

name: Bedford Park
note: 'Previously known as Bedford Park, the park was renamed after Brower in 1921.' Start = the Parks acquisition year 1892.

name: Brower Park
note: Renamed 1921 for George V. Brower, Commissioner of Parks for Brooklyn and Queens 1889-94 and 1898-1901, who died that year.

name: Winthrop Park
note: 'It was originally named Winthrop Park after an assemblyman, Col. Winthrop Jones, who acquired the land'. Start = the Parks acquisition year 1889.

name: Msgr. McGolrick Park
note: 'In 1941 the park was renamed for Monsignor Edward J. McGolrick'.

name: Seaside Park
note: Federal park today (OSM name; not a city property): 'In 1912, the city ... acquired the land for a park initially called Seaside Park and later Telawana Park.'

name: Jacob Riis Park
note: 'In 1914, the park was renamed for Riis.' Little was built before the bathhouse ('opened on August 6, 1932') and the Moses works of 1936-37; Naval Air Station Rockaway stood on part of it 1917-1930.

name: Mount Olivet Cemetery
note: Maspeth; 'founded in 1850' (OSM name; dated here because it is not a city property and not in parks.csv).

name: Lutheran Cemetery
note: Middle Village: 'Lutheran Cemetery traces its beginnings to 1852'. The change of name to (Lutheran) All Faiths Cemetery is put at 1990: ESTIMATED, year not read in a source here.

name: All Faiths Cemetery
note: Today's name (OSM). Rename year ESTIMATED (see previous row).

name: St. Michael's Cemetery
note: East Elmhurst; 'founded in 1852' (OSM name 'Saint Michael’s Cemetery').

name: Mount Hebron Cemetery
note: Flushing; Wikipedia infobox 'Established 1909' (first burial 14 April 1909 per the cemetery); begun in 1903 as the Jewish section of Cedar Grove Cemetery per that article — read through a search result.

name: Floyd Bennett Field
note: The airfield's name from its opening ('officially opened to commercial flights on May 23, 1931'); Naval Air Station New York 1941-71 kept the name in common use; National Park Service unit since 1972 (the OSM park outline carries the label).

name: Miller Field
note: Army airfield 'founded in November 1919 and completed in 1921', closed 1969; part of Gateway National Recreation Area since (the OSM park outline carries the label).

name: Prospect Park Plaza
note: Brooklyn: 'In 1867, the plaza was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux as a grand entrance to the Park'; 'originally known as Prospect Park Plaza'. (Point given: Manhattan has a Grand Army Plaza too.)

name: Grand Army Plaza
note: 'In 1926, the plaza, previously known as Prospect Park Plaza, was renamed Grand Army Plaza.'

name: St. John Cemetery
note: Middle Village; Wikipedia infobox 'Established 1879' (the article body gives no sentence). OSM name 'Saint John Cemetery'.

name: Fort Tilden
note: 'The fort was established as Camp Rockaway Beach shortly after the United States entered World War I in April 1917'; named for Samuel J. Tilden (year of the naming not given: label from 1917, ESTIMATED); 'an Army installation until the late 1970s, when it was decommissioned and made part of the Gateway National Recreation Area'.

name: Fort Wadsworth
note: '[Fort Richmond] was renamed Fort Wadsworth in 1865' (the whole reservation by General Order No. 16 of 4 February 1902); Navy 1979-95, then 'transferred to the National Park Service as part of the Gateway National Recreation Area in 1995' (the OSM park outline carries the label).
